subject: PhotonApps: sudden 5xx/429 burst - urgent escalation
messages:
From: Arman Gupta <arman@photonapps.com>

Subject: Production: Massive 5xx/429 spike starting ~07:55 PST

Team —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood endpoint for our inference calls beginning ~07:55 PST this morning. Error rates peaked around 30% for a 15-minute window and we're observing large client retry amplification from our side (clients retrying aggressively). Latency has jumped (p50 -> 1.2s, p95 -> 7.6s) and several requests are timing out end-to-end.

Attached are a trimmed set of traces and a logs dump: production-logs-2026-11-30.txt and 5xx-spike-traces.zip. The trace shows repeated 503 responses and many client retries causing backpressure.

Impact: several customer-facing endpoints degraded and we have an open support queue.

Can Redwood ops please:
- confirm if this is a capacity / autoscaling issue in our Dedicated pool
- advise immediate mitigation (throttle retries, fallback, cross-region failover)
- estimate ETA for stable window and whether SLA credit will be considered

We can temporarily pause automated retries on our side if you recommend it, but we need a short-term mitigation ASAP. This is high-priority for us.

—Arman
Arman Gupta, CTO
PhotonApps

Subject: Re: Production: Massive 5xx/429 spike starting ~07:55 PST

Quick update & preliminary analysis:

What I'm seeing: Dedicated pool (region: us-west-2) experienced a sharp depletion event. Autoscaler showed a surge of incoming requests that exceeded current pooled capacity while several instances were still cold-starting (GPU initialization ~45–60s). The combination led to transient 503/504s and 429s from queue saturation. We also observed retry amplification — many client retries re-queued while the scheduler was at capacity.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:00–09:15):
- Increased min-replicas for the affected pool from 3 -> 6 to provide headroom for the remainder of the peak window.
- Reduced scale-down aggressiveness (scale-down cooldown from 120s -> 600s) to prevent churning.
- Enabled warm pre-provisioning on the pool (start warm instances with a trimmed init profile).
- Deployed an edge token bucket limiter to smooth client retry bursts (throttled to 120 TPS per customer for PhotonApps).
- Opened failover route to hosted fallback model (smaller quantized variant) for requests that hit the queue timeout.

Short-term impact: error rate reduced from peak ~30% -> ~4–6% after changes, p95 latencies returned to ~1.5–2.2s for most traffic. We still see occasional 5xx during very short micro-bursts.

Next steps (15–90m):
- Keep min replicas elevated for the next 24h and monitor.
- Run post-incident sims to tune autoscaler thresholds (we likely need to lower target CPU/GPU utilization for this class of workload and add a warm-buffer setting).
- Hannah: would like an engineering decision on whether to make warm-prefill a default for Dedicated pools on high-throughput deals.

Attached: autoscale-metrics.png (short snapshot), truncated logs (production-logs-2026-11-30.txt).

—Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Arman — first, I'm really sorry for the disruption this morning. Thank you for the traces and patience. Quick summary of what we've done so far and what we recommend: 

What we did (today):
- Increased Dedicated pool min nodes and extended scale cooldowns to reduce churn.
- Enabled warm pre-provisioning and lowered cold-start penalty by trimming init hooks for the next 24h.
- Throttled retry amplification at the edge for PhotonApps while we stabilize.
- Failing fast to a quantized hosted model for non-critical calls to reduce pressure.

What we recommend (next 48h):
- We'll keep elevated min replicas for 24h and run a traffic replay to validate autoscaler thresholds.
- Schedule a joint postmortem (we propose Wed 12/2 10:00 PST) with technical owners — our SRE + your infra team.
- We will follow up with a proposed SLA credit calculation and a one-time service credit to offset customer impact.

Can you confirm if you're still seeing 5xx on any specific endpoints? If not, we'll mark this as stabilizing and track residual errors in the morning.

Thanks again — I'll prepare the customer-facing note and the credit calc and share before EOD.

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
